text:
James Hagens has not played since Nov. 5, when a cross-check to the back from Pittsburgh's Samuel Girard sent him out of the game in the third period. The Bruins put him on injured reserve two days later. On Nov. 21 he skated before the morning skate at TD Garden, an early step with no timeline attached, per Boston Hockey Now and Sports Illustrated. Boston Sports Journal's headline five days earlier summed up the wait: "Hagens absence is showing in Bruins lineup."

Before the injury, the seventh overall pick of 2025 was doing more than a rookie on 13.34 minutes a night has any right to: 6 goals and 12 points in 17 games, almost none of it on the power play. Some of it ran hot. He was shooting 17.6%, above the 13.8% our numbers think he can sustain, and his goals ran ahead of his 3.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances). But the chances were genuine, 1.03 expected goals per 60, a strong rate for any forward. When he returns, the thing to watch is whether he still gets to those spots after a back injury.
headline: James Hagens is back on skates, and missed
